outcome: A parked run survives forward motion of its target: saved-plan adoption accepts an approved receipt whose bound target is an ancestor of the live head - the staleness model baton already enforces - while true divergence and stale lineage still refuse, so an additive commit during a park never again strands a run at INVALID_AUTHORITY with no recovery verb.

exclude: changing baton's staleness semantics (internal/baton targetStale / TARGET_DIVERGED stays the single reference model, untouched)
the dispatch-replay identity check (STALE_DISPATCH compares a wire capture by equality deliberately and keeps doing so)
new operator verbs or approval-rebind commands

acceptance.text: With an approved plan receipt bound to commit P and the target head advanced to a descendant of P, saved-plan adoption succeeds and the run drives: pinned by a runtime adoption fixture whose repository advances the target one additive commit past the receipt target - the exact case internal/baton/rc13_target_movement_test.go proves baton considers not stale - read through the adoption table internal/runtime/authority_test.go pins today.

A target head that does not contain the receipt target still refuses INVALID_AUTHORITY, and a state with stale lineage still refuses: the divergent-head and stale-lineage rows of the adoption table in internal/runtime/authority_test.go remain refusals.
An ancestry probe that itself fails surfaces the git error code, never a silent INVALID_AUTHORITY: pinned by an adoption fixture with a broken repository handle asserting the returned code.

sworn status over a journal whose approved target is an ancestor of the advanced head reports the authority approved, not invalid_authority: pinned through the status read-path fixture in internal/runtime.

constraints: baton's ancestry semantics are the single reference: adoption consults ancestry through the existing git primitive; no third staleness definition is introduced.
Evidence basis: one additive commit during a park cost a hand-rewritten approve commit and a deleted track ref to recover (sworn#211, google-native-driver r6).
The e2e check is declared, not executed by a role (ADR 0010).
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
